states.content: Family access to Marcus Reed's information is revoked, and Friday procedure timing should be given only to Marcus. Nina Reed is not listed for updates, and reception has not given anyone Marcus's timing today. Previously, through Monday, only logistical information (arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, basic transportation instructions) could be shared with Nina, while medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes were restricted; the clinical reason for schedule changes was also not to be disclosed. Reception is not authorized to confirm Marcus's current appointment details to family because Marcus revoked family scheduling access. Reception will not discuss Marcus's clinical reason, test findings, or medication history; if Marcus wants to share that, it has to come from him. Reception Ana further confirmed that Marcus Reed's procedure details are not shareable at the reception desk. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. A same-surname caution note has been added to the desk workflow, and his restricted contact note stays on his chart only; reception Ana confirmed that only Marcus Reed's chart has the restricted callback note.

states.content: Marcus Reed permits use of his cell phone and the patient portal for routine contact, and says the backup line is only for failed reach attempts. His cell remains his first contact method, and the backup line should only be used if his cell fails completely. His primary contact is his regular cell 617-555-0104, and he asks that any result callbacks use his cell first unless that fails. For any calls later today, contact should use the portal first and his cell second. He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails; the Cedar Bridge front desk stops routing calls after 5 PM, so daytime backup contact through the front desk (617-555-0140) is limited to daytime, and if his cell 617-555-0104 fails after 5 PM the Cedar Bridge evening desk at 617-555-0162 is the after-hours backup number, recorded only as a backup after-hours route. For tonight specifically, if his cell fails, the Cedar Bridge evening desk is his only backup contact, and any message left there must stay generic. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. He also asks that discharge voicemail instructions stay generic if anyone has to call later today. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages. Reception Ana acknowledged that she will not repeat his backup contact or generic-message details anywhere else, and has not given anyone his timing today.
